figurative_meaning_bn: যার ছোঁয়া জল খেতে বাধা নেই
figurative_meaning_en: One whose touch does not prohibit drinking water
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে জলচল মানুষ, তাই তার স্পর্শে কোনো অশুচিতা হয় না।
গ্রামের পুরোহিত জলচল বলে সকলে তার কাছে জল নেয়।
example_sentences_in_english: He is a pure soul; his touch doesn't pollute anything.
The village priest is considered jalchôl, so everyone drinks water from his hands without hesitation.
history: This idiom originates from the historical Hindu caste system in Bengal, where touch purity determined social interactions, especially regarding water consumption among Brahmins and higher castes.
note: Refers to ritual purity in traditional Bengali society, less common in modern urban contexts due to social changes.
